critique: The black background, centered cyan-green burst, and clear outward expansion are aligned with the Ring Explosion intent. At 1.9s, however, the result still reads as a large turbulent spherical particle shell: broad interior ribbons, clumped bright knots, and dense webbing compete with the outer circumference. A cleaner explosive ring needs a more point-like origin and substantially less force-driven distortion so the perimeter remains the dominant readable structure. At 0.08s the source remains a tiny smooth glow rather than a visibly particulate ignition.

suggestions.why: Disable the main force field's position influence; its evolving displacement is producing the large folded interior ribbons and turbulent webbing instead of a clean radial explosion.
Collapse emitter X extent to concentrate the burst at the center rather than seeding a broad volumetric shell.
Collapse emitter Y extent with X so the late-stage particle distribution resolves primarily as an expanding ring.
Remove emitter Z extent to prevent depth-distributed particles from filling the ring interior and obscuring the perimeter.
Remove secondary-particle turbulence, which is reinforcing the noisy internal swirls and bright clumped arcs.
